mission_06: Stationarity is a fundamental assumption in time series analysis that requires the statistical properties of a series (mean, variance, autocorrelation) to remain constant over time. Most classical forecasting methods, including ARIMA, require the series to be stationary or made stationary through differencing. The Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test is the most widely used unit root test, where the null hypothesis is that the series has a unit root (non-stationary). The test regresses the first difference of the series on its lagged level and lagged differences, with a significantly negative coefficient indicating stationarity. The KPSS test takes the opposite approach, with the null hypothesis that the series is stationary around a deterministic trend. The partial autocorrelation function (PACF) measures the correlation between observations at a given lag after removing the effects of intermediate lags, computed efficiently using the Durbin-Levinson recursion. In this mission, you will implement autocorrelation, partial autocorrelation, the ADF test, and the KPSS test to comprehensively assess the stationarity properties of time series data.
